summary: This grid was lettered before it was numbered, and the record catches it changing its name: "B" street became Balboa and "C" street Cabrillo, Point Lobos Avenue became Geary, California Street South became Cornwall, and First Avenue became Arguello Boulevard. The Board spent twenty years accepting the roadways block by block, then started taking the width back off the pavements — Clement Street's roadway was widened four feet in 1926 by narrowing its sidewalks. Horses were kept here in quantity: forty behind 2934 Fulton Street in 1914, and a hundred and fifty at 701 Seventh Avenue in 1923. In 1914 the Board ordered the Geary Street, Park and Ocean Railroad to pull its cable tracks out of Fifth Avenue, calling them a public nuisance. In 1928 the Frank McCoppin School was allowed to rope off Seventh Avenue twice a day, half an hour at a time, on all school days. Under the houses went fuel oil, fifteen hundred gallons at a time, until about 1931. From 1983 the argument was about Clement Street itself: the Board barred new restaurants, fast-food places and bars between Arguello and Funston for a year, then barred banks there as well, then kept extending both. Since then the street has come back to the Board one licence at a time. Off it, the flats behind have been cut into condominiums ever since the late 1970s and the kerbs measured out foot by foot for permits and motorcycles. And in 2017 it decided, conditionally, not to rescind the tax sale of the common ground of Presidio Terrace, the private street inside the neighbourhood.
